So, a brigade was formed in Vitez, its headquarters were to be in Vitez, and also a brigade in Novi Travnik for the area of Novi Travnik. The reasons were the ones that I mentioned. We were unable to function in the previously mentioned way because the municipalities wanted to have a municipal brigade, because they wanted to take care of the logistics and with everything concerning the supplies. Nevertheless, in order for the commander of the Operative Zone, General Blaskic, in order for him to be able to issue such an order, formally, in such a form, and that means to appoint Mario Cerkez as brigade commander, he had to consult with the political leaders of Croats in Vitez. Otherwise, he would not have been able to do so, because under their pressure he had to change his first order, his first intentions being to have one brigade out of the soldiers from Vitez and from Novi Travnik. Also, he had to consult before he appointed somebody commander of the brigade of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, in the situation where it was obvious that there was call-ups of functioning of the central state institutions of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, is it your opinion that the municipalities took over the functions of the state and became small states by themselves? Do you think that the municipality took more authority than they would normally have, according to the law?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That is correct and that claim can be confirmed on many examples. After such a situation and after the central government was blocked in Sarajevo, in Central Bosnia the main authority were under the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you authenticate these two documents? Is this the signature of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, this is the signature of General Blaskic. The author of this command was Mario Rajic, and Stjepan Cervinac (phoen) had typed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher for the new batch of commands?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D243, D243A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at this document? On the 12th of March, Cerkez became the authority in the brigade, and the 18th of March he issued the following document. Could you first tell us whether this is the signature of Mr. Cerkez, the one that's on the second page?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, this is Cerkez's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me now read part of his first orders. 18th of March, 1993 he addresses a letter to the government of the HVO, the commander of the first battalion. "Owing to an increased incidence of overt destructive acts of individuals wearing HVO uniforms and insignia of members of HVO armed units, and with the aim of preventing such actions and enhancing combat readiness I hereby order"; and then comes orders the likes of which we have already seen. Does that mean that even in March you are still grappling with the same problems that you had in January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, we grappled with the same problems until the Washington Agreement. But I would like to clarify why this order was issued in the first place. You see, the commander of the newly established Viteska Brigade, that is Mario Cerkez, until his appointment as commander of this brigade, was in the joint brigade that was called Stjepan Tomasevic. When he took over this duty, aware of the key problems that existed in HVO units, and being aware, also, of the orders he had received from the commander of the Operative Zone as the commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, now being the commander of the Viteska Brigade, he actually is issuing the same orders that he issued as commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. But the brigade commander could not order the HVO government. Whoever drafted this document did so rather awkwardly. What he should have written was for the information of the HVO government, so that they should know what the military authorities were doing in relation to individuals engaging in destructive acts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're talking about the HVO government, do you mean the municipal government or some other government?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: At the time, at the level of the municipality, the HVO government was the highest form of organisation of the civilian authorities for the needs of a municipality. I am unable to give you an answer as to who constituted that government, because I was engaged in military matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D244, 244A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, the previous document, D243, issued by Mario Cerkez to inter alia, the commander of the first battalion had a registry number, record number, and now this, the commander of this first battalion, Anto Bertovic, says on the 19th of March, that is one day after Cerkez had issued his command: "In accordance with the order by the brigade commander number 01-18-1/ and," then illegible, "of 18 March, 1993, and owing to an increased incidence of overt destructive acts by individuals wearing uniforms and insignia of members of the HVO armed formations, and with the aim of preventing such actions and enhancing combat readiness, I hereby order"; and then he orders whatever we see in the text of the order. So, tell me, what does this document tell you in relation to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: From this document we can see that in the subordinate command, within the brigade, orders are being implemented, the orders that had been issued by the brigade commander. But the functioning of those relations, that is the chain of command, is something that I would like to speak of later on. But we can see that the brigade commander had carried out the command that had been issued by the commander of the Operational Zone, and this is going down lower in the chain of command. But also from this we can see how many criminal acts had happened in that area, maybe. In order to understand completely the situation related to these events, allow me, Mr. President, Your Honours, to tell you of an anecdote that was very topical at the time in the Lasva River Valley and in Central Bosnia. It is about the behaviour of the criminals. A bus that was going from Zenica was at some stage intercepted by a number of criminals that were wearing the HVO uniforms. So, they entered the bus and they asked money from the passengers. But the first passenger said to the soldier, "But I am a Croat," when he saw that the other one was wearing the HVO uniform. And this criminal answered, "But I'm not here to do a census, I'm just here to ask for your money.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm sorry if this is really not at level of this Tribunal. Thank you, Mr. President. Now, if you would allow me, we should now go onto a new batch of documents, but it is just one minute before the usual time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In that case we are going to stop now. Tomorrow we will start at a quarter to 10 and work until 13.30. So the hearing is adjourned until tomorrow morning.
